correctness.rationale: Equation (2) has diffusion coefficients proportional to the current abundances. At any strictly positive deterministic drift equilibrium the diffusion matrix is nonzero, so the constant equilibrium path is not an SDE solution. Exact translation produces a nonzero additive Brownian term at zero displacement. Equation (13) instead centers every diffusion coefficient at the deterministic equilibrium, and Equation (15) therefore has an absorbing zero solution. Itô's formula for squared displacement gives a strictly positive right derivative of the mean square at time zero for Equation (2), proving the model mismatch without simulation.

value.rationale: Mean-square stability near the positive equilibrium is a central advertised analytical conclusion of the article and is used to interpret noise tolerance. For the printed SDE, however, the deterministic positive state is continuously forced by Brownian noise and is not an equilibrium solution. Identifying the switch separates two scientifically different questions: stability of an explicitly centered auxiliary SDE versus fluctuation and stationary-distribution behavior of the abundance-proportional ecological SDE. This changes what Theorem 3.2 can legitimately support without challenging unrelated persistence or stationary-distribution results.
